chunks.text: Today, we will talk about Cusco.
Cusco is a city in Peru in South America.
It is a very old and beautiful city.
It was once the capital of the Inca Empire.
Cusco is high up in the Andes Mountains.
The air is thin and the views are amazing.
Let's learn more about this wonderful city full of history, color, and life.
Part two, where is Cusco?
Cusco is in southern Peru, about 3,400 meters above sea level.
It is surrounded by tall mountains and green valleys.
The city is built on old Inca foundations.
Cusco is far from the sea, but it feels alive with culture and history.
Many tourists come here before visiting Machu Picchu, one of the seven wonders of the world.
Cusco is known as the heart of the Inca world.
Part three, a short history of Cusco.
Cusco was the capital of the Inca Empire many centuries ago.
The Incas were great builders.
They made strong stone walls, temples, and roads.
When the Spanish arrived in the 1500s, they built churches and houses on top of old Inca buildings.
Today, you can still see both Inca stones and Spanish buildings together.
Cusco is like an open museum of history.
Part four, the main square, Plaza de Armas.
The center of Cusco is called Plaza de Armas.
It is a big and beautiful square.
There are two famous churches there, the Cusco Cathedral and Church of the Society of Jesus.
People meet, talk, and relax in the square.
There are shops, restaurants, and street musicians.
At night, the square is full of lights and laughter.
It is the heart of the city and a great place to start exploring Cusco.
Part five, Inca architecture.
Cusco is famous for its amazing stone buildings made by the Incas.
One example is Sacsayhuaman, an ancient fortress on a hill above the city.
The stones are huge, but they fit together perfectly without cement.
No one knows exactly how the Incas built them, but they are strong even after hundreds of years.
Walking through Cusco, you can see many old Inca walls still standing.
Part six, Machu Picchu.
Many people visit Cusco to see Machu Picchu, the lost city of the Incas.
It is about 80 kilometers from Cusco, high in the mountains.
You can take a train or hike the Inca trail to reach it.
Machu Picchu is full of temples, terraces, and stone houses.
It was hidden for many years and discovered in 1911.
It is one of the most beautiful and mysterious places in the world.
Part seven, the people of Cusco.
People in Cusco are warm and friendly.
Many of them are descendants of the Incas.
They speak both Spanish and Quechua, the old Inca language.
Traditional clothes are colorful with hats, ponchos, and woven fabrics.
People smile often and are proud of their culture and city.
They welcome visitors with kindness and joy.
Part eight, Food in Cusco.
Food in Cusco is delicious and full of flavor.
A popular dish is Lomo Saltado, made with beef, rice, and vegetables.
Another is alpaca meat, which is soft and tasty.
People also eat corn, potatoes, and quinoa, which all come from the Andes.
And don't forget to try mate de coca, a tea made from coca leaves.
It helps with the high altitude.
Part nine, Markets in Cusco.
Cusco has many colorful markets.
The most famous is San Pedro Market, near the city center.
You can buy fruits, bread, cheese, clothes, and souvenirs.
There are also handmade crafts, hats, scarves, and bags made from alpaca wool.
The market is full of smells, colors, and friendly voices.
It shows the real life of Cusco's people.
Part 10, Festivals and Music.
Cusco loves music and festivals.
The biggest festival is Inti Ramey, the festival of the sun in June.
It celebrates the old Inca sun god.
People wear traditional clothes, dance, and play drums and flutes.
There are also parades and ceremonies in the streets.
Music in Cusco is beautiful.
You can hear pamphlets and guitars everywhere.
Part 11, Nature around Cusco.
The nature around Cusco is breathtaking.
There are mountains, valleys, and rivers all around.
Many people visit the Sacred Valley, full of small villages and old Inca ruins.
You can also see Rainbow Mountain, a mountain with red, yellow, and green colors.
The air is cool and clear, and the views are unforgettable.
Cusco is perfect for people who love hiking and exploring.
Part 12, Goodbye from Cusco.
Thank you for listening to the Slow English Podcast.
I am Emily.
Cusco is a city full of history, life, and beauty.
It is a place where the past and present live together.
You can walk on ancient streets, eat local food, and meet kind people.
And if you go to Machu Picchu, you will feel the magic of the Andes.
Cusco is a city that stays in your heart forever.
Goodbye, or as people in Quechua say, Tupananchis Gama.
